Requirements/Graph visualization with the NVL suite

Requirement · high criticality

Graph visualization with the NVL suite

Render and interact with graph data in a React application using the NVL suite: the React binding, layout workers, interaction handlers and the dagre layout engine. Assess maturity, maintenance, licence, security and version compatibility across the suite, and identify alternatives if the suite fails a hard constraint.

Owner: dbs-amoswongCadence: 90 daysCreated 28 Oct 20265 candidates
Decision DeniedActive

Do not adopt @neo4j-nvl/react

Avoid. Proprietary licence, no published repository, no provenance, and a package that Node cannot load in either module system. The React binding is small; the cost is a 53 MB tree and a legal constraint.

Build vs buy scores the capability, not this package. A rejected package can still be a capability worth buying from a maintained alternative.

Constraints

  • Permissive license across the full dependency tree
  • React 18 and 19 supported
  • No install scripts in the dependency tree
  • No unfixed high or critical advisories
  • Actively maintained (release within 12 months)
  • Compatible versions across the NVL suite
  • If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap

Out of scope

  • Backend graph database and query language
  • Visual design and theming
  • Detailed benchmark against every non-NVL graph library

Decision rationale

The NVL suite fails the requirement's hard licence constraint. LICENSE.txt limits use to Neo4j Aura under the Cloud Agreement or commercial Neo4j under the Subscription Agreement; it is proprietary client software, not an OSI licence. The four NVL packages also publish no repository, carry no provenance across 390 versions, ship bundled code that cannot be reviewed, and cannot be loaded by Node in either module system because ESM syntax sits in .js files under commonjs packages with extensionless imports. The React peer range '18.0.0 || ^19.0.0' excludes React 18.2/18.3, and base pulls a Segment analytics SDK plus 43 MB of dependencies. @neo4j-bloom/dagre is MIT but is a 1-star fork of @dagrejs/dagre at 3.1.1, it is not used by layout-workers, and upstream is 3.1.3 — use @dagrejs/dagre directly if a dagre layout is needed. Open-source alternatives to evaluate for the graph surface: Cytoscape.js, Sigma.js, @antv/g6 and React Flow. Exception path: if the organisation holds an Aura or Neo4j Subscription agreement and accepts proprietary terms, revisit as a documented policy exception; even then, the Node/SSR packaging gap and the React 18 peer range remain. Version scope: the review targets 2.0.0. 1.2.2 was checked separately and has the same proprietary licence, missing source and provenance, bundler-only packaging and React 18 peer gap; its layout stack differs (cytoscape 3.33.1, @neo4j-bloom/dagre 0.8.14, mobx 3.6.2) and it installs 56.3 MB. The denial therefore applies to both 2.0.0 and 1.2.2.

Review timeline

  1. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/base Avoid Avoid. The renderer behind the suite: proprietary licence, no source, no provenance, 13 pinned dependencies including a Segment analytics SDK, and it touches document at import time.
  2. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/react Avoid Avoid. Proprietary licence, no published repository, no provenance, and a package that Node cannot load in either module system. The React binding is small; the cost is a 53 MB tree and a legal constraint.
  3. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/interaction-handlers Avoid Avoid. A 222 KB interaction layer over the proprietary renderer, with the same licence, source and provenance gaps and the same bundler-only packaging.
  4. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-nvl/layout-workers Avoid Avoid as part of the suite. Small and technically the cleanest package, but it carries the same proprietary licence, no source and no provenance. It depends on upstream @dagrejs/dagre, not the Neo4j fork.
  5. 28 Oct 2026 @neo4j-bloom/dagre Avoid Not needed. MIT and public, but a 1-star fork of dagrejs/dagre pinned at 3.1.1 while upstream is 3.1.3, and it is not used by the NVL layout-workers package. Use @dagrejs/dagre directly.
